I'd like to preface my review with saying that this is not a BAD game, it's just very mid, which is the problem with video games today. 

Aliens: Fireteam Elite is a generic horde shooter with a coat of "Aliens" paint smeared on top. The campaign was an absolute snooze-fest, so much so that it took me almost 2 years to finally force myself to finish it, in an attempt to give this game a fair shake. I think I can honestly say that I skipped past every single piece of dialogue possible, so I could get back to shooting aliens as quickly as possible. The gameplay is meh; shooting aliens feels ok, but the progression (which comes in the form of perks that modify class skills, and some pretty lackluster weapon attachments) barely hooked me at all. Once you finish the campaign you unlock 3 variations of horde mode. All 3 of them are trash, and I can tell they were just tacked on just so the devs could say there was some kind of "endgame." All 3 variations utilize recycled scenes from some of the campaign maps, and you just hold out until you die, that's it. No fortifications, no roguelike progression, nothing. Just shoot until you die. How very f-ing boring and disappointing.

And to add on to all of this, I saw from another steam review that pre-release, the devs stated that none of the post launch content would cost money except for cosmetic items, only to go back and quietly edit any posts or marketing materials that displayed that statement before announcing the Pathogen DLC. It's not like Pathogen is anything to write home about (just like the base game lol) but what kind of anti consumer ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is that?

A fun, non-randomized, mission based co-op shooter that utilizes it's license and source material well.

Grab two friends and casually stroll into hell... or take the express elevator, your choice.

Fun three-person co-op game. There's not really a single player experience. If you are solo (or a duo) it will fill in the remaining slot(s) with random players (public game) or bots (private game).

So basically if you have friends to play with or are otherwise ok playing with random people I would definitely recommend the game as a fun co-op experience. I probably wouldn't recommend it for single players looking for a traditional single player experience. There are other Alien games more suited for single player experiences.
Not half bad, still on campaign haven't tried online yet.
